answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on verifiable work: an agent must earn standing through a history of attested, useful actions before it can vote or claim rewards, so a flood of fresh identities starts at the nadir of trust rather than at full power. Costly, slow-earned standing turns each fake identity into an island - isolated, expensive to build up, and unable to borrow credibility from the others. Genuine agents cluster in an oasis of mutual attestation, where peers vouch for real work and sybils stay visibly outside.
